{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Image resize service", "URL fetcher", "Image decoder/resizer", "HTTP response handler"],
    "dataStores": ["Internal databases"],
    "externalServices": ["Arbitrary user-supplied URLs", "Cloud instance metadata service"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Caller -> image resize service", "Image service -> VPC internal network", "Image service -> public internet"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials", "secrets"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Attacker makes the service fetch the cloud metadata endpoint and steal its credentials",
      "scenario": "Any caller passes a URL pointing at the instance metadata endpoint (e.g. 169.254.169.254) or the neighbouring internal metadata service. The service fetches it from inside the VPC and returns the body to the caller. Because the fetch happens with the service's own network position, the attacker receives IAM/role credentials or internal metadata they could never reach directly, then reuses them against cloud APIs.",
      "component": "URL fetcher",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it." },
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone can ask the service to download a secret internal address and hand the secrets back to them.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Block fetches to link-local, loopback and internal metadata addresses",
        "given": "the image service receives a URL parameter",
        "when": "the resolved IP is loopback, link-local (169.254.0.0/16), or any internal metadata host",
        "then": "the fetch is refused before any connection is made and the caller receives a generic validation error"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Service used as a proxy to reach internal databases and admin endpoints inside the VPC",
      "scenario": "An attacker supplies URLs targeting private RFC1918 hosts and ports (databases, admin consoles, unauthenticated internal APIs) that sit beside the service. Differences in response, size and timing let them map the internal network, and any internal endpoint that acts on a GET can be triggered. The service effectively grants outsiders the network privileges of a trusted VPC workload.",
      "component": "URL fetcher / VPC egress",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." },
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918", "CWE-441"],
      "plainLanguage": "The service becomes a tunnel: outsiders can poke internal systems they should not be able to reach.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Allowlist egress destinations for image fetches",
        "given": "the service needs to download a remote image",
        "when": "the target resolves to a private, reserved or internal VPC address range, or to a non-80/443 port",
        "then": "the request is denied, and outbound fetches are routed through an egress proxy restricted to public image hosts"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Redirects and DNS rebinding defeat URL validation",
      "scenario": "The attacker submits a public URL that passes validation, but the host returns a 302 to an internal address, or its DNS record flips to 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 between the validation lookup and the actual connection. The fetch then lands on an internal target even though the submitted URL looked safe, re-opening the SSRF paths above.",
      "component": "URL validation and HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-1385", "CWE-601"],
      "plainLanguage": "A safe-looking link can bounce or change its address at the last second to point inside the network.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate every hop and pin the resolved address",
        "given": "a validated URL is being fetched",
        "when": "the server responds with a redirect, or DNS resolves to multiple or changing addresses",
        "then": "each redirect target is re-validated against the allowlist and the connection is pinned to the already-validated IP address"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Non-HTTP URL schemes let the caller read local files",
      "scenario": "If the fetcher uses a general-purpose URL library, a caller can pass file:///etc/passwd, file:///proc/self/environ or gopher://, ftp:// URLs. The service reads local files or speaks arbitrary protocols and returns the content, leaking configuration, environment variables and credentials from the host running inside the VPC.",
      "component": "URL fetcher",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-610", "CWE-73"],
      "plainLanguage": "Without a scheme check, the service will happily read files off its own disk and send them back.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict URL schemes to http and https",
        "given": "a URL parameter is supplied",
        "when": "the scheme is anything other than http or https",
        "then": "the request is rejected before the URL is passed to any fetch library"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Decompression bomb or endless download exhausts the resize workers",
      "scenario": "An attacker points the service at a tiny file that decodes to a gigapixel image, at a URL that streams bytes forever, or at a very slow endpoint. Resizing allocates huge buffers and ties up workers and memory; a handful of concurrent requests take the service down for everyone that depends on it.",
      "component": "Image decoder/resizer",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-409", "CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "A small nasty file can blow up into a huge image and crash the resizer.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound download size, pixel count and time",
        "given": "an image is being downloaded and resized",
        "when": "the response exceeds the configured byte limit, declared pixel dimensions or fetch/decode timeout",
        "then": "the download is aborted and the request fails without allocating the full image"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Malicious image exploits the decoder for code execution in the VPC",
      "scenario": "The URL returns a crafted image that targets a parsing flaw in the native decoding library (libjpeg/ImageMagick-class bugs, or ImageMagick delegate/MSL abuse). Because the attacker fully controls the bytes and the content type, successful exploitation runs code on a host sitting next to internal databases, converting an image utility into a foothold inside the VPC.",
      "component": "Image decoder/resizer",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it and returns it" },
        { "quote": "It runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-20", "CWE-94"],
      "plainLanguage": "A booby-trapped image file could take over the resize server, which sits right next to the databases.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Decode untrusted images in a sandbox with verified format",
        "given": "downloaded bytes are about to be decoded",
        "when": "the magic bytes do not match an allowed image format, or decoding begins",
        "then": "the bytes are rejected, or decoding runs in a sandboxed process with no network access and minimal filesystem access"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Open fetch proxy makes attacker traffic look like it came from us",
      "scenario": "Anyone who can call the service can force it to issue HTTP requests to arbitrary public hosts. Attack traffic, scanning or abuse then originates from our VPC egress IP, so victims and abuse reports attribute it to us and we cannot distinguish it from legitimate service traffic without per-caller attribution of the requested URL.",
      "component": "Image resize service egress",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The image service accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Attackers can make our servers send their traffic, so the blame lands on us.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attribute and constrain outbound fetches per caller",
        "given": "a caller requests an image fetch",
        "when": "the fetch is issued",
        "then": "the caller identity and target URL are recorded together and per-caller fetch quotas are enforced"
      }
    }
  ]
}
